shape: a district name read as a project name
input: A Port Authority Bus Terminal replacement filing whose body says 'hudson yards' once and nothing else about the Western Rail Yard.
assertion: bestTargetForClustering returns null. 'hudson yards' is districtWide, so it never establishes identity, whatever the record is about.
origin: 19 records and 15 buildings clustered into one project: Manhattan West and the Port Authority Bus Terminal were absorbed by the district term.

shape: a verdict read as a decision
input: Four records: three 'filed' and one 'under construction' that is neither attributed to the project's own site nor corroborated by a second record.
assertion: provenStage returns 'approved' or lower and reports the refused stage. A single borrowed record cannot advance a project.
origin: Manhattan West Phase 4's 'substantial completion' raised the whole Hudson Yards project to under construction. Two records of twenty-two carried the stage and neither was the project.

shape: a mention read as a subject
input: A record titled 'DisneylandForward Project' whose body mentions ocvibe once, as a cumulative project in an EIR.
assertion: bestTargetForClustering picks the target named in the TITLE. A body mention never outvotes the record's own subject.
origin: One term each, so the tie broke on declaration order in targets.ts and OCVibe is declared before Disney.

shape: a capture date read as an event date
input: A record with no deadline and no published_date, captured today.
assertion: bestDate returns null. first_seen is never a fallback, so a dateless record cannot become a project's most recent activity.
origin: A dateless LinkedIn post captured 2026-08-10 outranked six dated stories about a county approval published 2026-07-21.

shape: an applicant's company name read as a venue word
input: A project whose rolled-up venueType is 'Integrated Resort' and whose records never use the word resort.
assertion: deriveProjectName does not put the venue word in the name. A venue word enters a name only when a record uses that word.
origin: Nine projects carried a venue word no record supports.

shape: a zoning code read as a venue
input: 'USE PERMIT for a daycare and school in a CR (Commercial Resort) Zone, with waivers of development standards for a trash enclosure.'
assertion: classifyVenueType returns null. The venue classifier reads the same neutralised text the gate reads, so boilerplate that cannot admit a record cannot classify it either.
origin: The same filing was stored as venue_type Resort and then named the project 'Buona Vita resort'.

shape: borrowed entitlement vocabulary admitting an out-of-vertical matter
input: Nine out-of-vertical filings - daycare, elementary school, place of worship, medical office, self-storage, car wash, distribution center, trash enclosure, cell tower - each carrying real entitlement vocabulary (use permit, mixed use, site plan).
assertion: governmentGate refuses every one. Entitlement vocabulary is not a subject.
origin: A daycare and school use permit reached a generated client document as 'Buona Vita resort'. See the note in the report for the two terms this case deliberately does not cover.

shape: a filter that fails open and returns the parent set
assertion: Zero projects, never the parent set. An unresolvable facet fails closed.

guard.needle: an unresolvable ${u.axis} must return the empty set, not the parent's rows

origin: market=Atlantis returned all 254 United States projects, which is the shape a client scope narrowed to one market would have shipped.

shape: a filter that fails open and returns the parent set
input: venue=Notavenue and category=Notacategory on the register.
assertion: Zero projects on every axis, not only market.
origin: Same shape as the market case, found on the other two axes when they were measured for the first time.

shape: a filter that does its parent's job
input: United States > California > Anaheim, walked by project id across every page.
assertion: L3's ids are a strict subset of L2's, and strictly fewer. Compared by id, not by count.

guard.needle: so the market filter is not being applied

origin: L3 Anaheim returned 27 and L2 California returned 27; both 'changed' against a global baseline, and the two being the same number meant nothing to a count-only audit.

shape: an All that is not all
input: The All chip on the stage, venue and category axes.
assertion: Each equals the register total, including the projects with no value on that axis.

guard.needle: An "All" that is not all is a silent gap

origin: All venues read 203 against a register of 267 and offered no route to the missing 64.

shape: a count answering a different question from the control it labels
input: Every market node in the rail, in California, Nevada and New York.
assertion: The number on the node equals the number clicking it returns.

guard.needle: A navigation tree that hides a reachable result, or promises one it cannot produce, is not navigation.

origin: Orange County and Willets Point read 0 over a project the click returned; Yonkers read 1 and returned none.

shape: a period scope applied to a property of the project
input: A project first seen in July that gained a record captured in August, under Arrived, August.
assertion: It appears. Arrived resolves through the records, not through projects.first_seen.
origin: A month in which Clark County captured 81 records and Anaheim 79 rendered as an almost empty register.

input: A scoped client's generated document, compared project by project against the database's own resolution of the same scope.
assertion: Equal sets on every axis, not merely fewer projects than the unscoped register.

guard.needle: the composer and the database disagree about this scope

origin: The composer dropped the venue, category and stream axes entirely, so a client scoped to attractions was sent everything.

input: Miami-Dade County, whose Legistar feed has published nothing since 2018-06-15.
assertion: Declared in lib/dead-feeds, excluded from every client document, and the exclusion is counted in the document.

guard.needle: every frozen one is declared in lib/dead-feeds

origin: Two markets sat on the covered list for years while frozen, because health asks whether a source produced and not whether what it produces is still moving.

input: Every rule that removes a project from a document: frozen market, dormant, hollow, provisional name, detail cap, no filing in the period, unplaced.
assertion: The document states the count and the reason for each. A rule that removed something and said nothing fails the audit.

guard.needle: every rule that removed a project from a document is stated in that document

origin: Thirty-nine projects were held out of every report on their name alone, and no document said so.
